statement_summary: SP 800-171 program for every CUI system, documented in policies, standards, SSP, and POA&M
Security Manager designated program lead; vCISO for strategy
CUI only in the enclave; boundary changes approved and in the SSP and inventory before use
Annual risk assessment using SP 800-30
Risk acceptance authority by level; DFARS and export failures never accepted
Annual policy review; standards set measurable minimums
Written, risk-rated, time-limited exceptions
Sanctions for noncompliance
Annual SP 800-171A self-assessment; co-sourced audit; monthly POA&M review; SPRS updated within 30 days; affirmation on evidence
Cloud providers FedRAMP Moderate or equivalent; every ESP documented with its CRM
No CUI to a supplier without DFARS flowdown and verified SPRS and CMMC status
Security and CMMC scoping review before an acquired site or system handles CUI
AI tools approved through P10 before use; no CUI in AI outside the enclave
Baselines and change control for every in-scope system, including the shop floor
Monthly scanning of every in-scope system; remediation timelines; unsupported software replaced or isolated
Security documentation kept 6 years
Unique accounts; no shared logins (Plant 2 exception to 2027-01-31)
U.S.-person confirmation before enclave or ITAR data access
Role-based least privilege with approvals; program-edit rights for programmers only
MFA for all; hardware keys for administrators; phishing-resistant for all enclave users by 2027-01-31
Same-day disablement at termination; credentials the person knew are changed
Prior access removed within 5 business days of a transfer
Quarterly access reviews; 45-day inactivity disable
Privileged access through the broker with separate accounts; inherited accounts reviewed within 30 days of an acquisition
Lockout, session lock, and session termination settings
Remote access only through the virtual desktop gateway
Vendor remote access only through the broker with MFA and recording; vendor tools prohibited
Password rules; credentials vaulted and rotated
No CUI on external systems outside the assessed boundary; public AI blocked
No wireless on enclave VLANs; enterprise authentication where wireless reaches in-scope systems
Incident response plan and runbooks with crisis, response, and plant roles
Immediate reporting of suspected incidents by all workforce
MSSP escalation within 30 minutes; discovery time recorded
DIBNet report within 72 hours; two certificate holders; incident number to the prime
Images and monitoring data preserved 90 days from the report; image before rebuild, including shop-floor systems
Malware to DC3, never to the Contracting Officer
Export control decision for any possible release of CUI
Counsel-directed investigation and privilege labeling
Annual exercises covering exfiltration with DIBNet drill, shop-floor ransomware, and supplier incidents
All in-scope systems log to the SIEM; 1 year searchable, 6 years archived
No ransom payment without CEO decision, counsel, insurer, and OFAC check
Supplier incidents reported to the company; coordination with the prime
Lessons learned within 14 days; documented within 30
Four classification levels with handling rules
CUI banner and distribution statement on company-created CUI; MES templates at both plants
CUI only in approved enclave locations recorded in the data flow register
FIPS-validated encryption at rest and in transit on every path
Printed CUI in cabinets, covered on visitor routes, sealed and logged in transport
Locked shred bins with certificates; sanitization before media leaves
Only labeled, inventoried, encrypted USB drives at the 8 legacy machines
Encrypted isolated backups; quarterly restore tests; recovery objectives from the BIA
Public release review by trade compliance
Services customer data separated per customer and reviewed quarterly
Business use; monitoring notice
No CUI on personal devices, personal accounts, corporate systems, or commercial email
Approved AI tools only; no CUI in public or corporate AI; numeric rule
Awareness, CUI handling, insider threat, and role-based training
Report phishing, lost devices, unescorted visitors, and misuse at once
Visitors signed in, badged, and escorted; no photography; foreign-national visits announced
Remote work with CUI only on enclave devices in a private space
No user-installed software
Annual acknowledgment
